attestation.basis: 14942 graded forecasts of 14942 recorded on the ledger (mean scores: no numeric mean scores); graded record only, no calibrated out of sample evaluation has been attested, so this engine's numbers are published as uncalibrated scores, never as probabilities

probability_rendering.reason: no calibrated out of sample attestation on record for this engine; its numbers may be published only as uncalibrated scores, never as probabilities

excluded_variant: One variant is left out on purpose: saying whether a gap fills early in the session or only by the close. The within-day price record on hand cannot support it today, so it is not promised.

explanation.body: Its forecast takes this form: probability and distribution, over same session, graded at that close. It is graded on a score that rewards probabilities that land close to what actually happens. It would be ended if after 120 index gaps, fill-probability Brier is no better than the unconditional per-band base rate. It counts as proven at 120 index gaps.
explanation.summary: At the open, stake a set of chances on today's gap for every name that gaps at least half a percent, and be graded on it at today's close.

failed_gap_sub_claim.acceptance_proxy: Acceptance for the live session is read from the first minutes record where it covers a name: the closing location inside the first 15 minute range, read in the gap's direction, from Alpaca SIP 5 minute bars (first_minutes.py). Names and sessions the record does not cover keep the daily proxy, the closing location inside the session's own daily range, labelled per entry as daily_proxy. Each live entry names its own acceptance_source.

first_minutes_record.source: Alpaca SIP 5 minute bars, first 30 minutes after the open, via first_minutes.py

failed_gap_sub_claim.grading: Each live leg is written to the public record under its own forecast quantity and graded on its own outcome, the close against the prior close, apart from the fill chance scores. Its cases are never counted on top of the main record's cases.

history.label: Descriptive history over the whole panel, not a walk-forward proof: the proxy is read from the same session it describes.

failed_gap_sub_claim.statement: A stated sub claim of this engine, graded separately from the fill chances: when the session rejects a gap (acceptance below half), the close is forecast to finish on the other side of the prior close, the failed gap travelling the other way, not merely failing to fill. When the session accepts the gap, the close is forecast to finish on the gap's own side. At exactly neutral acceptance the leg makes no direction call.

ancestor.note: The older pane's own published figures, from within-day prices over 90 days, any gap however small, for the three index funds only. A different method from this page's daily figures, shown so the two are never mixed up. A later run of that study sits on the studies record with slightly different totals, because it is a later run; the two runs are not compared here.

history.label: History, not live forecasts
history.note: Worked out day by day over the price history on record: each day's chances were built only from earlier days, then checked against what actually happened that day. These are study figures from the past, not the live record.

idea: The older Gap-Fill Pane shows how gaps like today's behaved in the past. This page does a different job: at the open, for every name that gaps at least half a percent, it stakes a set of chances on today's gap before the session unfolds, writes that set to a public record that cannot be edited afterwards, and is graded at today's close.
kill_criterion: This tool is retired if, after 120 graded index gaps, its fill chances score no better than simply using the plain rate for that gap-size band every time.

shifters.fear_note: Judged on the completed session before the gap day, because a fear reading for a day is built from that day's close and cannot be known at the open. Gauge readings are on record from 2024-11-04 to 2026-11-04; the session before this gap day (2026-11-03) carries one, so its gauge parts were judged too.
shifters.vol_note: This reading needs a fear gauge close for the completed session before the gap day. That session (2026-11-03) carries one, and the reading is in the top third of the readings on record, so it counted. The last gauge reading on record, 2026-11-04, was 16.61, not in the top third of the readings on record.

live_record.second_arm: A second form of this engine, built on each name's own past gaps instead of everyone's, is written down as part of this engine and starts only once the pooled record above has matured. It is not a separate tool, and its cases will never be counted on top of these.
